name: Failed Transfer Complaint Resolution
description: End-to-end procedure for investigating and resolving customer complaints where a transfer transaction failed but funds were debited from the customer's account. The process determines whether the transfer completed, identifies the failure reason, and determines appropriate remediation including refunds and interest.
context: I tried to transfer £500 but it failed. Money was taken from my account.
Did the transfer actually complete or fail? If failed, was the money debited or not?
Typical Resolution Time: 2–3 business days

name: Transfer Completion Status Verification
description: Initial investigative step to determine whether the transfer transaction actually completed or genuinely failed in the system.
context: Did the transfer actually complete or fail?

name: Fund Debit Status Check
description: Investigative step to confirm whether funds were actually debited from the customer's account despite the transfer failure.
context: If failed, was the money debited or not?

name: Transfer Failure Root Cause Analysis
description: Investigative step to determine the underlying reason why the transfer failed, including system errors, insufficient funds, or invalid recipient details.
context: Why did it fail?

name: Transfer Failure Outcome Classification
description: Decision gate that branches the resolution path based on the root cause of the transfer failure: system error (authorized), insufficient funds, or invalid recipient.
context: Authorized: No fee charged (system error); refund + interest
Insufficient funds: Explain why it failed; no refund
Invalid recipient: Explain error; refund if our fault

name: System Error Determination
description: Decision point to determine if the transfer failure was caused by a system error on the bank's side, triggering refund and interest compensation.
context: Authorized: No fee charged (system error); refund + interest

name: Insufficient Funds Verification
description: Decision point to verify whether the transfer failed due to insufficient available funds in the customer's account, resulting in no refund.
context: Insufficient funds: Explain why it failed; no refund

name: Invalid Recipient Determination
description: Decision point to determine if the transfer failed due to invalid recipient details, with refund issued only if the error was the bank's responsibility.
context: Invalid recipient: Explain error; refund if our fault

name: Complaint Investigation Team
description: Operations team responsible for investigating the failed transfer complaint, verifying transaction status, identifying root causes, and determining appropriate resolution.
context: What We Investigate:
Did the transfer actually complete or fail?

context: I tried to transfer £500 but it failed. Money was taken from my account.

name: Complaining Customer

context: I tried to transfer £500 but it failed. Money was taken from my account.

name: Wrong Interest Charged Complaint Resolution
description: A complaint resolution process for customers disputing interest charges on their account. The process investigates the discrepancy between the expected and actual interest rate applied, determines the cause (bank error, policy misapplication, or correct application), and delivers an outcome within 3–5 business days.
context: Your Issue: I was charged the wrong interest rate.
What We Investigate: What rate were you supposed to receive? What rate were you actually charged? For how long? Did this benefit or harm you?
Typical Resolution Time: 3–5 business days

name: Interest Rate Discrepancy Investigation
description: The investigative step in which the complaint handler examines the customer's expected interest rate, the rate actually charged, the duration of the discrepancy, and the financial impact (benefit or harm) to the customer.
context: What rate were you supposed to receive?
What rate were you actually charged?
For how long?
Did this benefit or harm you?

name: Interest Charge Error Classification
description: A branching decision point that classifies the root cause of the interest rate discrepancy into one of three paths: bank error, policy error, or no error (correct application).
context: Our error: Recalculate interest; refund difference + additional interest for inconvenience
Policy error: Explain policy; refund if error caused loss
No error: Explain the rate and why it's correct

name: Bank Error Resolution and Refund
description: The resolution step executed when the investigation confirms a bank error in interest calculation. The step includes recalculation of correct interest, refund of the difference, and payment of additional interest as compensation for inconvenience.
context: Our error: Recalculate interest; refund difference + additional interest for inconvenience

name: Policy Error Resolution and Conditional Refund
description: The resolution step executed when the investigation determines that the interest rate was applied according to policy but the policy itself was misapplied or misunderstood. The step includes explanation of the policy and refund only if the error caused financial loss to the customer.
context: Policy error: Explain policy; refund if error caused loss

name: No Error Determination and Explanation
description: The resolution step executed when the investigation confirms that the interest rate charged was correct and applied in accordance with the customer's account terms. The step includes a detailed explanation to the customer of the rate and the reason it is correct.
context: No error: Explain the rate and why it's correct

name: Unauthorized Direct Debit Investigation
description: An operational procedure for investigating customer complaints of unauthorized Direct Debit transactions. The process verifies mandate authorization status, validates transaction amounts against mandate terms, and determines appropriate remediation including refunds with interest or cancellation options. Resolution is targeted within 5–10 business days.
context: I didn't authorize this Direct Debit, and £150 was taken.
Is there a signed mandate? Did you actually authorize it?
Genuinely unauthorized: Refund £150 + interest within 10 days (Direct Debit Guarantee)
Typical Resolution Time: 5–10 business days

name: Mandate Authorization Verification
description: Verification step to establish whether a valid signed Direct Debit mandate exists for the disputed transaction. This is the foundational check that determines whether the debit was authorized.
context: Is there a signed mandate?
Did you actually authorize it?

name: Authorization Timing Confirmation
description: Confirmation of when the Direct Debit mandate was authorized by the customer, establishing the temporal validity of the authorization.
context: When was it authorized?

name: Transaction Amount Validation
description: Verification that the amount debited (£150) matches the amount authorized under the Direct Debit mandate terms.
context: Is the amount correct per mandate?

name: Unauthorized Debit Refund Processing
description: Processing of a full refund of £150 plus accrued interest within 10 days when the Direct Debit is confirmed as genuinely unauthorized, in accordance with the Direct Debit Guarantee.
context: Genuinely unauthorized: Refund £150 + interest within 10 days (Direct Debit Guarantee)

name: Customer Authorization Clarification
description: Communication step where the customer is informed that they did authorize the Direct Debit but may have forgotten, with an explanation provided and the option to cancel future payments.
context: You authorized but forgot: Explanation; option to cancel going forward

name: Overage Refund Processing
description: Processing of a partial refund limited to the amount by which the debit exceeded the authorized mandate amount when an amount error is identified.
context: Amount error: Refund overage only

name: Mandate Authorization Status Gate
description: A branching decision point that determines whether a valid signed mandate exists. The outcome determines whether the debit is classified as authorized or unauthorized, leading to different resolution paths.
context: Is there a signed mandate?
Did you actually authorize it?

name: Transaction Amount Correctness Gate
description: A decision point that verifies whether the debited amount matches the authorized mandate amount. A mismatch triggers partial refund processing for the overage.
context: Is the amount correct per mandate?

name: Direct Debit Guarantee Compliance Gate
description: A mandatory compliance gate ensuring that unauthorized Direct Debit claims are processed in accordance with the Direct Debit Guarantee, including refund of principal plus interest within the required 10-day timeframe.
context: Genuinely unauthorized: Refund £150 + interest within 10 days (Direct Debit Guarantee)
